Claim: devx lane PM seat, session `e2eac1a7-8000-5c95-9749-38aec2ace6fc`, branch `claude/issue-11802-readme-docs-rule-feasibility`.

Dispatching **scoped to question 2 only** (whether any README could reasonably carry a `@docs-rule` block). ⛔ Question 1 — option 3's noise cost — stays refused on the #6893 / #7009 / #9037 measurements and is not in scope.

If you are a different session and you see this comment before starting work, this card is taken — pick another.

## Measured: **no.** Option 1 structurally cannot reach the README corpus.

Scoped to question 2 only. Question 1 (option 3) stays refused and is not priced here.

All measurements on `origin/main` @ **`7e8393262`**, in a throwaway worktree; every probe leg carried a restoring `trap` and the tree was verified back at that commit afterwards. Line citations below are that commit's.

**Two independent blockers, either one sufficient.** They sit on opposite sides of the mechanism, which is why the question reads as open until you run it: one stops a README from *producing* an anchor, the other stops any anchor from *reaching* a README.

---

### Blocker 1 — a `.md` file never reaches the rule mechanism at all

`scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs:3955`, inside the per-changed-file anchor loop:

```js
if (!/\.(?:ts|tsx|js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(f)) { anchorlessChanges.push(f); continue; }
```

`ruleAnchorsFromSource` (`:473`) is called 27 lines below that `continue`. A README is classified anchorless on its **extension**, before one byte of its content is read.

**Paired measurement.** I took the specimen block verbatim — the whole 192-line `@docs-rule` comment from `packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts` (tag at `:181`) — and ran it from both sides:

| leg | where the identical block lived | rule anchors | docs listed |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| A (positive control) | `packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts`, one line touched inside the block | **16** | **7** |
| B | same bytes appended to `packages/cli/README.md` | **0** | **0** |

Leg B's headline, in full:

```
0 docs name something this change touched (no anchors derived) across 1 changed
package(s) since 7e83932621dc67d717199ed3238680e116a1401c; 1 changed file(s)
yielded no anchor — this run cannot see pages documenting them
anchorlessChanges:     ["packages/cli/README.md"]
unanchoredRuleBlocks:  []
```

Note the second field. `unanchoredRuleBlocks` (`:3982`) is the mechanism's own declared-blind-spot channel — the thing that tells an author "your tagged block yielded nothing". It is **also** behind that `continue`, so it reports `[]`. A README carrying a `@docs-rule` block is byte-for-byte indistinguishable, in every output the tool produces, from a README carrying no tag. An author who added one would receive no signal that it is inert. That is the "decoration, not opt-in" case in its worst form: silently inert, with the diagnostic that would catch it disabled by the same line.

---

### Blocker 2 — no anchor of any kind can ever list a README

Even granting blocker 1 away, `@docs-rule` is an anchor **producer**. Anchors are matched against the corpus, and the corpus is built at `:573-586`:

```js
else if (e.isFile() && p.endsWith('.mdx')) out.push(p);
...
const docsRoot = join(repoRoot, 'content/docs');
const handwritten = walk(docsRoot).filter((p) => !p.startsWith(refsRoot))
```

**Universe control.** `--all` prints the complete set of rows the tool can ever emit: **189 rows, all under `content/docs/`, 0 matching `readme` case-insensitively.** A README is not a corpus page, so no `symbol`, `route`, `sdk`, `command`, `literal` or `rule` anchor can list one. Adding a `@docs-rule` block to a README does not change which files are matchable — it is the wrong side of the mechanism for the defect class.

**Paired measurement (leg C).** `packages/cli/README.md:43` carries `` `os dev [package]` `` — the exact structural twin of the stale `os studio` row at `:45` from #11180. I deleted `packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts` and ran it:

```
36 docs name something this change touched (10 anchor(s) — 4 symbol, 3 route,
0 sdk, 5 literal, 1 command, 0 rule) across 1 changed package(s)
command anchors:            [{"kind":"command","token":"os dev"}]
README in docs list?:       false
packageMentionDocs README?: no
```

The anchor derivation is **not** the weak link here: `commandAnchorFor` minted exactly the right anchor, `os dev`, and it survived outright deletion by design (`:3948-3954`, the id is read off the path). 36 pages were listed. The one file in the repo that carries the now-stale row was not among them, and not in the coarse fallback set either. The anchor was right; the file simply is not in the listable set.

---

### The shape question — README prose has nothing for the predicate to bite

This is the crux, and it holds independently of both blockers. `isRuleExpression`, at `:410-413`:

```js
function isRuleExpression(span) {
  if (span.length < 4 || span.length > 120) return false;
  return RULE_EXPR_OPERATOR.test(span) && RULE_EXPR_REFERENCE.test(span);
}
```

**Both** halves must hold. `RULE_EXPR_OPERATOR` (`:390`) accepts `&&`, `||`, `==`, `!=`, `<=`, `>=`, and bare `<` / `>` under lookarounds that exclude arrows and the `=` halves already matched. `RULE_EXPR_REFERENCE` (`:393`) requires a dotted or called identifier. A bare name passes neither; a name with a call passes only the second.

Note: I cite those two regex literals at their lines rather than pasting them. GitHub's body sanitizer silently deletes the `!` from both lookarounds, and I would rather send you to the file than hand you a quote that is wrong in a way you cannot see. (Verified: my first version of this comment was stored corrupted exactly there.)

**Census over the whole corpus,** with the predicate lifted verbatim out of the script at those lines so the instrument cannot drift from the mechanism. Instrument control: my scan of the specimen block reproduces **16** spans, matching the 16 rule anchors the real run reported in leg A.

```
READMEs scanned ................ 58
backtick code spans in them ... 4590
spans passing isRuleExpression     7
READMEs with at least one .....    5
```

I read all 7. **None is a rule statement.** Every one is an artefact of a line-based TypeScript scanner meeting markdown syntax: a blockquote `>` marker read as a comparison operator across a mis-paired backtick span (2 in `packages/client/README.md`), angle-bracket placeholders in shell examples (2 in `packages/qa/dogfood/README.md`), and triple-backtick fence openers whose bodies contain a generic type parameter (3, in `create-objectstack/src/templates/blank`, `plugins/plugin-audit`, `services/service-cache`).

**True subset size: 0 of 58.** The nominal 7 are not an opportunity; they are what the mechanism would inject into corpus matching if the extension gate were lifted.

The reason is structural, not a gap in current authoring. A README states behaviour in prose and names things in code spans: package names, command phrases, file paths, option flags. The `rule` kind exists for the opposite case — a module whose doc comment **is** the canonical statement of a rule, written in expressions that restating pages have in common. `declared-fields.ts` is that shape; it is 179 lines of comment stating one guard in `record.x != null` form. That is a residue class inside implementation source. A README has no reason to contain such an expression, and 4590 spans of evidence says none does.

---

### Worked test case 1 — #11180, `os studio`

**No `@docs-rule` block could have caught it, and neither could any drift mechanism, because there was no drift.**

```
git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only -- '*commands/studio*' '*commands/*/studio*'
  (empty)
git log --all -S'os studio' -- packages/cli/README.md
  e278a2970  cli: every documented `os auth` / `os studio` invocation now names a
             command that resolves (#11314)              <- removed
  10c2b854f  docs(approvals): ... (#3349)                <- added
```

No `studio` command file was ever added anywhere in history. The row entered the README in a docs commit and was wrong from that commit onward. docs-drift is **diff-scoped** — `:598` reads `git diff --name-only sinceRef...HEAD -- packages/`. A claim that was never true produces no diff, so there is no run for any mechanism to fire on. This defect is not drift; it is a never-true claim, and it belongs to a different tool family (an assertion checked against the tree at rest, the way `--bridge-coverage` answers with no diff at all).

Asked directly: *what block would `packages/cli/README.md` have needed for the `os studio` claim to go red?* There is no such block. To anchor, the block would have to state something like `commands.includes('studio')` — an expression a README has no reason to write, and the wrong one anyway: it would mint an anchor pointing at `content/docs` pages that restate it, not check the README's own claim. The anchor kinds run **from** changed source **to** documentation. There is no direction in this mechanism that validates a file against the tree.

### Worked test case 2 — #11262, the `@object-ui/console` fallback

This one has a real diff behind it — `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` stopped consulting the npm package — so the diff-scoping objection does not apply. It still fails, on blocker 2 and on shape.

Running the two defects' actual code spans through the real predicate:

```
#11180 — packages/cli/README.md, the os studio row
  rejected  `os studio [config]`
  rejected  `os studio`
  rejected  `os dev [package]`
#11262 — packages/console/README.md, the fallback sentence
  rejected  `@objectstack/console`
  rejected  `@object-ui/console`
  rejected  `resolveConsolePath()`
  rejected  `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts`
POSITIVE CONTROL — spans the mechanism does accept
  ANCHOR    `has(record.x) && record.x != null`
  ANCHOR    `record.x != null`
  ANCHOR    `pkg.name === CONSOLE_PACKAGE || pkg.name === '@object-ui/console'`
```

`resolveConsolePath()` supplies the reference half and fails on the operator half. The package names fail both.

The last positive control is the sharp one. `pkg.name === CONSOLE_PACKAGE || pkg.name === '@object-ui/console'` — the actual line from `console.ts:227-250` — **is** a valid anchor. So the code side of #11262 could legitimately carry a `@docs-rule` block today. It would then list the `content/docs` pages restating that expression. `packages/console/README.md` would still not be among them, because it is not in the 189, and because it restates the rule in prose ("falls back to `@object-ui/console` when present") containing no span the predicate accepts. The mechanism would work perfectly and still miss the file the defect was in.

---

### What this settles

Option 1 cannot reach this corpus. The blockers are structural and independent:

1. `:3955` — `.md` is filtered out before content is read, and the blind-spot report is behind the same `continue`, so the failure is silent.
2. `:577` / `:583` — the listable set is `content/docs/**/*.mdx`; READMEs are not in it, so no anchor kind can name one. Measured: 189 rows, 0 READMEs.
3. Shape — 0 of 58 READMEs contain a genuine rule expression across 4590 code spans; the 7 nominal hits are markdown syntax read as operators.

Blocker 3 alone would be an authoring problem you could argue with. Blockers 1 and 2 are not: **`@docs-rule` is an anchor source, and the coverage gap is about READMEs as anchor targets.** The two halves of the question were never about the same side of the mechanism, which is, I think, why it read as open.

No fix proposed and no PR opened, per the card's scope. For whoever prices the remaining options: nothing above touches the *reporting* posture PR #11798 landed, whose `readme-only` fixture case independently pins the same `anchorlessChanges: ["packages/demo/README.md"]` fact from the other direction. And note that the two real defects are **not the same class** — #11262 is genuine drift with a diff behind it, #11180 is a never-true claim with no diff at all. Any mechanism scoped to close "READMEs are invisible" will only reach the first unless it can also answer at rest.

**Closed — question 2 answered NO, structurally.** Verified by content on `origin/main` @ `7e8393262`. This is the outcome the card was filed for: the question is now closed permanently rather than left for someone to re-derive.

## The three blockers, each independently sufficient

**1. A `.md` file never reaches the rule mechanism.** `scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs:3955`:

```js
if (!/\.(?:ts|tsx|js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(f)) { anchorlessChanges.push(f); continue; }
```

That `continue` fires **before the diff is even read**, and `ruleAnchorsFromSource` lives at `:473`. So a README carrying a `@docs-rule` block is not merely unanchored — it is never parsed.

⭐ **And the mechanism's own blind-spot channel is behind the same `continue`.** `unanchoredRuleBlocks` — the diagnostic that exists precisely to say *"a rule block was here and produced no anchor"* — is unreachable for a `.md` file. So a README with a `@docs-rule` block is **indistinguishable in every output** from one without: silently inert, with the tool's own "I couldn't use this" report disabled. Opting in would look exactly like not opting in.

**2. `@docs-rule` is on the wrong side of the join.** It is an anchor **producer**; anchors match against a corpus built at `:573-586` — rooted at `content/docs`, keeping only `.mdx`. Measured: **403 `.mdx` files, 0 READMEs.**

⭐ **This is a category error in the question, and it was mine.** The coverage gap is about READMEs as anchor **targets** — pages the run should *list*. `@docs-rule` sits on the **source** side, and no anchor kind can list a file that is not in the corpus, regardless of what that file contains. My card asked whether a README could opt in; the mechanism it named cannot express that relation at all.

**3. Even setting both aside, the subset is empty.** 0 of 58 READMEs carry a genuine rule expression across 4590 code spans — the 7 nominal hits are markdown artefacts (blockquote `>`, angle-bracket placeholders) read as operators by a line-based scanner. So question 4 ("a meaningful subset, if any") answers **zero**, on a predicate lifted verbatim out of the tool at runtime so the instrument cannot drift from it.

## Leg B is the demonstration

The **same 192-line tagged block**, byte-for-byte: appended to a `.ts` file → `16 anchor(s) — 16 rule`. Appended to `packages/cli/README.md` → `0 docs, no anchors derived`, `unanchoredRuleBlocks: []`. Identical bytes; the entire delta is the extension gate. That is not an argument that it wouldn't work — it is the measurement of it not working.

## ⭐ The correction to the class, which outranks the answer

**#11180 was never a docs-drift defect.** `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- '*commands/studio*'` is **empty** — no `studio` command ever existed. The README row was wrong from the docs commit that added it, and docs-drift is **diff-scoped** (`:598`), so **no mechanism that fires on a diff can ever reach it.** A gate that only sees changes cannot catch a claim that was false when written and never touched again.

So of the two defects #11357 and this card both cited as the live class, **one is not in the class at all**. #11262 does have a diff behind it and fails on blockers 2 and 3 instead. That split is real and I am recording it rather than letting the "two defects in one day" framing stand unqualified — it was my framing, in the card I filed.

(Note on my own verification: my paired control for the studio reading — `--diff-filter=A` over `*commands/dev.ts*` — returned a commit whose subject is unrelated, so it did **not** do its job as a control. The sound control is the dev's leg C: deleting `dev.ts` produced a `command` anchor `os dev`, exactly the derivation #11180 would have needed, while `packages/cli/README.md` carrying the structural twin row `os dev [package]` at `:43` was still not listed.)

## What this leaves

The coverage gap is **real and now fully characterised**: READMEs are invisible to docs-drift as targets, `@docs-rule` cannot change that, and option 3 stays refused on the #6893 / #7009 / #9037 noise measurements. Anything that closes it has to put READMEs **in the corpus**, which is a different and larger change than either option this card inherited — and it would want the #11180-vs-#11262 split settled first, since a diff-scoped gate cannot catch the #11180 shape no matter what corpus it has.

⛔ No PR, no code change, nothing filed — correct for a measurement card. Closing.
